paper_title: Bridging Cognition and Emotion Empathy-Driven Multimodal Misinformation   Detection
caption: Results of Ablation Study
model_annotation: The bar chart presents the results of an ablation study comparing the accuracy (%) of a proposed misinformation detection model across two datasets—PHEME and PolitiFact—under various ablated conditions. On the vertical axis, accuracy is plotted from 75.0% to 95.0% in increments of 2.5%, while the horizontal axis lists five experimental conditions: “Ours” (the full model), “w/o comments,” “w/o text,” “w/o select,” “w/o emotion,” and “w/o cognition.” The chart is split into two panels: the left panel for PHEME and the right for PolitiFact. In PHEME, the full model (“Ours”) achieves 89.84%, followed by “w/o comments” at 86.82%, “w/o text” at 80.10%, “w/o select” at 88.80%, “w/o emotion” at 87.34%, and “w/o cognition” at 87.17%. In PolitiFact, “Ours” reaches 90.57%, “w/o comments” 85.85%, “w/o text” 83.02%, “w/o select” 89.62%, “w/o emotion” 84.91%, and “w/o cognition” 87.74%. Each bar is color-coded: “Ours” in dark red, “w/o comments” in orange, “w/o text” in yellow, “w/o select” in light blue, “w/o emotion” in medium blue, and “w/o cognition” in dark blue. The chart visually demonstrates that removing text has the most detrimental effect on performance in both datasets, while the full model consistently outperforms all ablated variants.
